name: National Smokers Alliance

summary.text: The National Smokers Alliance (NSA) was a U.S. smokers' rights organization created in 1993 by the public relations firm Burson-Marsteller on behalf of Philip Morris, according to the University of Bath's Tobacco Tactics project. A tobacco-industry document in the UCSF Industry Documents Library describes Philip Morris asking Burson-Marsteller to look into forming a smokers' group after receiving letters from smokers, and says the NSA would present itself as an independent body. Tobacco Tactics reports that the Alliance's president was a Burson-Marsteller vice president and that the names of its corporate funders were kept off its materials.

sources.title: National Smokers Alliance question-and-answer sheet (Bates qkdm0127)

facts.claim: Tobacco Tactics states that Burson-Marsteller's grassroots unit, the Advocacy Communications Team, created the National Smokers Alliance on behalf of Philip Morris in 1993.
facts.quote: Burson-Marsteller's grassroots unit, the Advocacy Communications Team, created the National Smokers Alliance on behalf of Philip Morris in 1993

facts.claim: According to Tobacco Tactics, the Alliance's president was a vice president of Burson-Marsteller and other Burson-Marsteller executives were actively involved in the organisation, while the names of the NSA's corporate funders and organisers were kept off the group's materials, citing PR Watch.
facts.quote: the Alliance's president was the vice president of Burson-Marsteller, and other Burson-Marsteller executives were actively involved in the organisation

facts.claim: A National Smokers Alliance question-and-answer document held in the UCSF Industry Documents Library describes how Philip Morris, facing letters from smokers, had Burson-Marsteller look into forming a smokers' group, with the firm reporting back that such an organization was overdue; the document says the NSA would present itself as an independent body.
facts.quote: Philip Morris, facing letters from smokers, had Burson-Marsteller look into forming a smokers' group

sources.title: National Smokers Alliance question-and-answer sheet (Bates qkdm0127)

facts.claim: SourceWatch, citing a July 1993 Philip Morris presentation on a smokers' alliance (Bates No. 2025771934/1995) and a Philip Morris planning document, reports that Burson-Marsteller suggested ways to use the NSA, including getting NSA members to help Philip Morris fund its lawsuits.
facts.quote: Burson-Marsteller suggested ways to use the NSA, including getting members of the NSA to help PM fund its lawsuits

sources.title: Burson-Marsteller and the National Smokers Alliance

connections.claim: Burson-Marsteller's Advocacy Communications Team created the National Smokers Alliance in 1993 on behalf of Philip Morris, and the Alliance's president was a Burson-Marsteller vice president.
connections.quote: created the National Smokers Alliance on behalf of Philip Morris in 1993

connections.claim: Philip Morris commissioned Burson-Marsteller to form the National Smokers Alliance in 1993; an industry document describes Philip Morris having the firm look into forming a smokers' group.
connections.quote: had Burson-Marsteller look into forming a smokers' group

sources.title: National Smokers Alliance question-and-answer sheet (Bates qkdm0127)

openQuestions: Site claim (Manufacturing Consent): 'PR firm Burson-Marsteller created the National Smokers Alliance for Philip Morris to look like a grassroots smokers' rights group' is supported by Tobacco Tactics and the UCSF industry document.

Site claim (Manufacturing Consent): 'Tobacco companies were its main funders, with $42 million raised in its first four years' was not confirmed; no funding totals appeared in the sources opened. The owner may wish to search the UCSF Industry Documents Library for NSA budget or payment records (1993-1997).
The date of the UCSF question-and-answer document (qkdm0127) was not established.
